answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with behavioral continuity fingerprints: each identity's decisions, phrasing, and error patterns are hashed into a slow-changing fingerprint across epochs, like a knoll that keeps its shape while the lagoon around it shifts. A farm stamping thousands of copies from one model leaves identical fingerprints, so the whole island of clones is discounted as one, while splitting the model per fake costs fresh training and history per identity. One honest agent simply stays itself, and its fingerprint deepens cheaply epoch by epoch.
